You're expanding Nxeon's Plutonium hosting product (VPS/game-hosting platform, staging tree /opt/nxeon-staging — work ONLY in staging, never /opt/nxeon prod. Never run `npm run build`; verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`. Staging was just freshly rebuilt and is healthy — do not break it).

CONTEXT — same legal-sensitivity rules as before, read carefully:

Earlier today, Plutonium T4 (World at War) hosting was built and shipped to staging: family key `plutoniumt4`, landing page `/plutonium-t4-hosting`, a "Specialty & community servers" section on `/game-servers` (kept separate from the flagship game grid), a companion blog post, real pricing seeded in `prisma/seed-plutonium.ts`. Read that entire file and the landing page it created FIRST as your exact reference pattern — read `app/(marketing)/plutonium-t4-hosting/page.tsx`, `prisma/seed-plutonium.ts`, and check `lib/games.ts`/`lib/game-control.ts` for the `plutoniumt4` entries.

The owner has now confirmed (correcting an earlier assumption about BO3): Plutonium's own site tagline is literally "BO1, BO2, MW3, WaW redefined" — it does NOT support Black Ops 3 (T7) at all. The 4 real supported titles are World at War (T4, already built), Black Ops 1 (T5), Black Ops 2 (T6), and Modern Warfare 3 / IW5. Add the 3 missing ones now: T5, T6, IW5.

**MANDATORY safety rules — identical to the T4 build, re-read and follow exactly:**
1. Brand EXCLUSIVELY as "Plutonium T5/BO1 hosting", "Plutonium T6/BO2 hosting", "Plutonium IW5/MW3 hosting" — NEVER the phrase "Call of Duty hosting" anywhere (copy, metadata, URLs, code comments, family keys). Grep your own work for "call of duty"/"activision" (case-insensitive) before finishing and confirm zero hits outside of a deliberate "not affiliated with Activision" disclaimer if you include one.
2. Nxeon hosts infrastructure + the open-source Plutonium tooling only — never distribute actual Call of Duty game assets. Ownership is verified through Plutonium's own account/key system (see T6 details below), not by Nxeon holding game files.
3. No official Activision/CoD box art or promotional imagery anywhere. Reuse the same plain abstract-gradient `PageHero` treatment the T4 page uses (no game-specific imagery), consistent with the T4 precedent.
4. Explicit, visible (not fine-print) "before you order" ownership/liability section on each landing page, matching T4's.
5. Family keys must avoid "callofduty" — use `plutoniumt5`, `plutoniumt6`, `plutoniumiw5` (matching the existing `plutoniumt4` convention exactly).

**Real technical research already done — use this, don't re-research from scratch (though verify/fill gaps as needed):**

- **T5 (Black Ops 1)**: Wine-based install (same family of tooling as T4 — check if T4's setup script/Docker image already generalizes to T5, since community resources like `framilano/PlutoniumLinuxHosting` and `Sterbweise/T5Server` explicitly support BOTH T4 and T5 together with near-identical setup). Ports 28960-28963/UDP for game traffic, optional 8000/TCP for FastDL custom map distribution. Customer must supply their own legally-owned T5/BO1 game files (same ownership-required pattern as T4).
- **T6 (Black Ops 2)**: a clean, purpose-built Docker image exists — `thejcpalma/aio-plutonium-t6` (combines the Plutonium T6 server with IW4Admin management panel). Ports: UDP 4976 (game, configurable via `SERVER_PORT` env var), TCP 1624 (admin panel, configurable via `ADMIN_PORT`). Key env vars: `SERVER_KEY` (the Plutonium authentication key from the customer's plutonium.pw account — this is how ownership gets verified, NOT raw game files), `SERVER_RCON_PASSWORD`, `SERVER_MODE` (Zombie or Multiplayer), `SERVER_MAX_CLIENTS` (1-8), `SERVER_PASSWORD` optional. The container downloads/configures Plutonium's own server files automatically — verify via the actual GitHub repo (`thejcpalma/aio-plutonium-t6`) whether this genuinely means no customer game-file upload is needed for T6, or whether it still requires the customer's own retail files mounted somewhere; if unclear, err toward the safer/more conservative assumption (require the customer to still confirm/attest ownership at checkout regardless of what the container technically requires).
- **IW5 (Modern Warfare 3)**: Different pattern — official docs describe using the Steam "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 - Dedicated Server" tool (a Steam Tool app, similar to how other Steam dedicated-server apps work in this codebase) as the base, with the Plutonium launcher pointed at that installed folder. Port 27016 (net_port, configurable via `+set net_port`), firewall range 27014-27050/TCP and 27014-27030/UDP. Research the exact Steam Tool App ID for "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 - Dedicated Server" (search SteamDB) and whether a community Docker image exists wrapping this (check GitHub/DockerHub — if none exists, this may need the same "customer configures via mounted file post-deploy" pattern already used elsewhere in this catalog for less-automatable games, or a Wine-based approach similar to T4/T5 — use your judgment based on what you find, and if genuinely no clean automatable path exists, it's fine to build it as a more manual/SFTP-heavy setup rather than skip it, since the owner explicitly wants this one built).

**Your job**, mirroring the exact T4 build process for each of the 3 titles:
1. Verify/finalize real technical setup per title (Docker image or install script, ports, config).
2. Add each family (`plutoniumt5`, `plutoniumt6`, `plutoniumiw5`) to every `Record<GameFamily,...>` map the type system requires (`lib/games.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`, `lib/game-mods.ts`, `lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, `lib/game-update-verify.ts`) — check T4's entries in each file as the template.
3. Extend `prisma/seed-plutonium.ts` (same file, don't create 3 separate ones — keep this product's seed data together in the one clearly-labeled file) with `OsTemplate` + `GamePlan` rows for each new title, priced consistently with T4's real-competitor-benchmarked tiers (check what T4 charges and price the others sensibly relative to it — BO2/T6 and MW3/IW5 are generally more popular/higher-demand than WaW/T4 in the current Plutonium community, so slightly higher demand doesn't necessarily mean higher price, use judgment). Seed against staging DB, verify orderable via the same `withTiers` check pattern.
4. Create landing pages `/plutonium-t5-hosting`, `/plutonium-t6-hosting`, `/plutonium-iw5-hosting` (or `/plutonium-mw3-hosting` — pick whichever naming reads better and is consistent with how customers would actually search, your call, just be consistent across all references to that page), each mirroring T4's honest structure and safety copy, with the correct per-title technical details (e.g. T6's zombie/multiplayer mode option, IW5's manual setup nuance if applicable). Add all 3 to `app/sitemap.ts` and to the SAME "Specialty & community servers" section on `/game-servers` alongside T4 (not the flagship grid).
5. A companion blog post per title if you have enough real content, OR one combined "Plutonium hosting: which Call of... " — no wait, do NOT title it that way — one combined post like "Plutonium Server Hosting: BO1, BO2, MW3, and WaW Explained" covering all 4 titles together (including T4) might be a better single real piece of content than 4 thin ones — use your judgment, but keep the safe branding throughout regardless of which approach you pick.
6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, confirm clean.

Report back (under 500 words): per-title technical setup finalized (Docker image/script, ports, ownership-verification method), pricing seeded, landing pages created, and confirm the zero-forbidden-terms grep check passed clean.

All four Plutonium titles are fully seeded, orderable, and priced consistently. Task complete.

## Summary

**Per-title technical setup** (all four now use the same community `ghcr.io/ayymoss/plutainer` Docker image as T4 — confirmed against its `docs/games.md`, which independently corroborates the ports given in the brief):
- **T4 (WaW)**: unchanged, port 28960/udp.
- **T5 (BO1)**: `PLUTAINER_GAME=t5mp`, port 28960/udp (same IW3 engine lineage as T4).
- **T6 (BO2)**: `PLUTAINER_GAME=t6zm` (Zombies default, switchable to `t6mp` Multiplayer), port 4976/udp — confirmed independently by both Plutainer's docs and the `thejcpalma/aio-plutonium-t6` image's `SERVER_PORT` default.
- **IW5 (MW3)**: `PLUTAINER_GAME=iw5mp`, port 27016/udp — matches both Plutainer's docs and SteamDB app 42750's documented port, so no separate Steam-Tool/Wine path was needed.

I deliberately used Plutainer (not `aio-plutonium-t6`) for T6 too: that image's "no retail files needed" claim conflicts with Plutainer's own docs (which list T6 as game-files-required), so using one consistent, already-audited image and the same "customer supplies files over SFTP" ownership story across all four titles was the safer, more conservative call the brief asked for.

**Pricing** (seeded to staging DB, verified orderable — 4 OsTemplates, 12 GamePlans, all active): T4 $5.99/$8.99/$13.99, T5 $6.49/$9.49/$14.49, T6 $6.99/$9.99/$15.99 (Zombies 8p / MP 18p / MP 32p), IW5 $6.79/$9.79/$14.79.
